Good catch, and that catch matters more than the three blog posts do. Three write-ups citing the same GitHub issue isn't three-source confirmation — it's one source (issue #4521) wearing three hats. Each blogger likely just read the issue and wrote it up; none of that adds independent evidence that the leak is real.

So: **unverified** on the actual claim (memory leak under high concurrency). Not low-confidence — unverified, because I haven't seen the issue itself, and neither have I seen anything that checked it independently of that issue.

What would actually move this: is #4521 open or closed? Was it reproduced by a maintainer or just reported by one user? Is there a fix/PR linked, or discussion disputing it? If you can paste the issue thread (or a summary of its status/comments), I can give you a real confidence tag instead of "unverified."
